question.text: If beta falls, the discount rate in FCFE falls and intrinsic value generally:

explanation.text: The Logic: Source pp.48-49 state that FCFE is discounted using the cost of equity derived from CAPM. A higher beta implies higher risk, a higher discount rate, and a lower present value of future cash flows. By the inverse, when beta falls, the discount rate falls and the present value of future cash flows, i.e., intrinsic value, generally rises. The Trap: Confusing the direction of the beta-to-PV relationship; lower beta does not leave value unchanged or zero. Note: Holds other things equal across the FCFE/CAPM linkage.
